findings.quote: relieved the Achaeans of their gravest problem
findings.problem: τοὺς δ᾽ Ἀχαιοὺς ἀπέλυσε τοῦ μεγίστου προβλήματος: πρόβλημα is a thing thrown up in front, a bulwark or barrier (here Corinth/the Isthmus defence), not a 'problem' in the modern sense. 'Problem' makes the Achaeans simply benefit; the Greek says Cleomenes freed (stripped) them of their greatest bulwark, which then paradoxically gave them the pretext of the next sentence.
findings.proposed_fix: relieved the Achaeans of their greatest bulwark

units.note: The Greek of the sentence is compact and the irony is Polybius's; the fix keeps the word-level sense of πρόβλημα. Final sentence truncated at [...] in both Greek and English, matching.

findings.quote: the killing of fellow citizens he treats as the gravest impiety, deserving the heaviest penalties
findings.problem: τὸ γε τοὺς πολίτας ἀποκτεινύναι μέγιστον ἀσέβημα τίθεται καὶ μεγίστων ἄξιον προστίμων: τίθεται is passive/impersonal (is held, is regarded), a general opinion, not a view attributed to the historian or to Phylarchus.
findings.proposed_fix: the killing of fellow citizens is held to be the gravest impiety, deserving the heaviest penalties

findings.quote: In the one, what governs is plausibility, even if it be false, because the object is the deception of the spectators; in the other it is the truth
findings.problem: ἐν ἐκείνοις μὲν ἡγεῖται τὸ πιθανόν ... ἐν δὲ τούτοις τἀληθές: ἐκεῖνοι = tragedy (plausibility), οὗτοι = history (truth). After 'the latter ... the former' in the preceding sentence, 'the one/the other' can be read the wrong way round.
findings.proposed_fix: In tragedy, what governs is plausibility, even if it be false, because the object is the deception of the spectators; in history it is the truth

units.note: The preceding 'latter = tragedy, former = history' is correct; only the following 'the one/the other' is at risk of inversion.
